main_text.p: סִיבוּתָא, סִיבוּת, סִיבוּ Chald. Idem. Syr. ܣܝܒܘܬܐ Idem, ad Hebr.11.12. Lucæ 1.36. Plur. cum Affixo יְמֵי סִבְוָתֶיךָ Dies senectutis tuæ, Psal.103.5.

סוּג Ch. Incedere, recedere, currere. Hinc Elias deducit illud, כּוּלְהוֹן מְסַגְּנָן בִּרְעוּת נַפְשְׁהוֹן Omnes discurrut in voluntate animæ suæ, Jer. 8.6. Deinde סִיג est Sepire, obsepire: & metaphoricè Ordinare, constituere: Ab Heb. שׂוּךְ.
סִיגָא, סִיגָּא Ch. & Syr. Sepes, sepimentum, maceria, paries. Plur. סִיגֵּי Et in locum sepium, Lucæ 14.23.
סִיגָא Ch. Idem, Prov. 24.31. Vide quoque supra in סִיגָא. סִיג Ch. Scoria, purgamentum, rejectametum, Pl. סִיגִין.

סוּחַ Syriac. Velle, desiderare, cupere: convenit cum ܨܒܐ. Præt. ܨܒܝܢ In quo acquiescit anima mea, Matth. 12.18. Pahel Part. ܨܒܝ Desiderabat, Joh. 8.56. Pl. cum Aff. ܨܒܝܢ Desideramus, 2. ad Corinth. 5.8.1. ad Thess. 2.8.
ܨܒܐ Syr. Voluntas, Animi promptitudo, 2. ad Cor. 8.11.
סוּט Ch. Ferre, afferre, portare. Præter. סָטֵי מְשַׁקּוּלְתָּא Apportat perpendiculum, Thren. 2.8. Alii, Extendit. Aphel אוֹסִיט Idem. Levit. 11.25.28. Jon.
סוּךְ Ch. Ungere, inūgere, inungi. Ithpeh. אִתְסָךְ Idem.

page.notes: Hebrew, Syriac and Chaldee forms are transcribed as far as legible; several vocalised forms in the scan are blurred and may differ in points. The catchword is a Hebrew word at the lower right. The Syriac and Hebrew forms are approximate where the print is faint.
